# GpuFanController v1.7.0

The initial public release of a personal project built to cool two NVIDIA Tesla
V100 datacenter GPUs. It combines autonomous Arduino Nano firmware, a C++ Ubuntu
daemon and **FanCtl**, a mouse-enabled terminal configuration/monitoring utility.
The version continues the project's development numbering.

## Highlights

- **Nano-owned cooling:** up to two GPU fan groups per controller, with two fans
  sharing PWM in each group and four independently monitored tachometers. The
  host forwards temperatures; the Nano owns speed control and safety decisions.
- **Calibrated RPM curves:** up to four temperature/RPM points, a nine-point
  calibration table, measured startup/running PWM limits and optional verified
  fan-stop. Calibration preserves the last good results on abort and confirms
  successful EEPROM storage.
- **Headless-friendly FanCtl:** mouse and keyboard operation over SSH or locally,
  draggable curve points, live Status, a multi-controller Overview and alert history.
  One Save changes review covers daemon and Nano settings, including GPU labels.
- **NVIDIA and experimental AMD support:** NVIDIA temperatures use a persistent
  NVML session in an isolated helper, avoiding per-sample process/context startup;
  AMD uses native Linux `amdgpu` edge-temperature sensors without ROCm. Mixed
  vendors and multiple Nanos can be managed by one daemon.
- **Low-idle-overhead daemon:** workers sleep until data, serial activity or a
  deadline needs attention, preserving temperature freshness and safety timing.
- **Controls and alerts:** group enable/disable, expected-fan selection, Auto and
  timed Full-speed/Off modes, thermal/RPM/current/supply thresholds and optional
  Ubuntu motherboard-speaker notifications for critical faults.
- **Conservative failure handling:** ten seconds without temperature packets
  commands both groups to 100%. Invalid readings also trigger Nano protection.
  Failed GPU queries get three attempts with 250 ms between attempts; retained
  readings keep their original three-second freshness limit. Ordinary Auto output
  ramps smoothly; calibration, startup and safety outputs bypass the ramp.
- **Setup resources:** illustrated user manual, schematic, printable fan mount,
  and an optional reviewed assistant for initial GPU-derived thermal thresholds.

## Compatibility

- **Host:** Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 with systemd. NVIDIA needs working drivers and
  NVML (`libnvidia-ml.so.1`) plus `nvidia-smi` for discovery/setup metadata; AMD
  needs a readable native `amdgpu` edge sensor. Intel and legacy
  AMD `radeon` drivers are not supported.
- **Controller:** classic ATmega328P Arduino Nano, firmware **1.7.0**, serial
  protocol **2**, EEPROM schema **5**. Nano Every/ESP32 boards are not supported.
- **Existing development installations:** migrate the `/usr/local` installation
  before installing the `.deb`; do not mix installation methods.
- **Firmware upgrades:** the packaged updater accepts compatible registered
  controllers from firmware **1.5.0** onward, backs up/verifies EEPROM, and does
  not rewrite the bootloader. Earlier/unknown formats and downgrades require manual
  review. Existing 1.5.x-or-later calibration does not need repeating solely for
  this update; older unmeasured tables do not establish measured minima or stop.
- Host installation preserves existing host configuration and does not flash the
  Nano. GPU labels require a scan and confirmed save when no label is stored.

## Installation

Download this release's installer, inspect it, then run it as your normal user:

```sh
curl --fail --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
  https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/releases/download/v1.7.0/install.py \
  --output gpu-fan-install.py
# Inspect gpu-fan-install.py before running it.
python3 gpu-fan-install.py --version 1.7.0 --start
```

The installer invokes sudo for package/service operations. A Nano update is
optional, separate and explicitly confirmed; it is never automatic. Stop GPU
workloads and supervise cooling during restarts, calibration and firmware uploads.

See the [installation, migration and recovery guide](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.0/docs/RELEASES.md)
and [illustrated FanCtl manual](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.0/docs/USER_MANUAL.md).
Release assets are the Ubuntu `.deb`, `install.py`, `release.json` and
`SHA256SUMS`; the package contains the application firmware and hardware documents.

## Known limitations and validation

- The author's hardware setup uses **four ARCTIC S4028-15K fans**, **two NVIDIA
  Tesla V100 GPUs**, an old-bootloader Nano clone and one INA3221 with R100 shunts.
  This is not certification of other GPU variants, wiring or airflow arrangements.
- AMD support has automated fixture coverage but **has not been validated on
  physical AMD hardware**. Hotspot/junction and memory temperatures are not used
  as substitutes for the selected NVIDIA core / AMD edge sensor.
- WSL is useful for development, but USB/IP attachment and GPU-driver access add
  dependencies. A stopped WSL distribution cannot forward temperatures; retries
  do not guarantee recovery from driver or USB faults.
- Fans share PWM per group. Individual fan switching is unavailable; Off/Disabled
  requests 0% PWM, **not a 12 V power cut**, and may not stop every fan model.
  Current is measured per fan pair, not individually.
- The communications timeout is **not a hardware reset watchdog**. Hardware
  watchdog reset is not enabled for the current old-bootloader Nano.
- Multi-device saves are coordinated, not atomic across the host and every Nano.
  Inspect partial/unconfirmed results before relying on changed settings.
- Automated host, firmware-policy, serial-emulator, terminal and release-tooling
  tests cover software behavior. The release workflow builds/tests the code and
  checks package installation in an isolated Ubuntu container; it does not test
  physical cooling. Validate actual airflow and temperatures under supervised load.
- The REST API is localhost-only and trusts local non-browser clients; do not
  expose it directly to the network.

## Safety and support

This is a quick personal project, released because it may be useful to others—not
a supported cooling product. Software, firmware, schematic and mount are provided
**as is**, without guarantees that they will work correctly or safely with your
hardware. Failures, wiring mistakes or unsuitable settings can cause overheating,
hardware damage, data loss or downtime. You are responsible for validating cooling.

Focused pull requests are welcome, but I may not respond, review or merge them.
Issues and Discussions are disabled; this is not a support service.
See the [risk notice](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.0/README.md#use-at-your-own-risk),
[MIT license and liability disclaimer](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.0/LICENSE)
and [support policy](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.0/SUPPORT.md).
